title: The Four Pawns, the Averbakh and the h3 systems
intro:
# The Four Pawns, the Averbakh and the h3 systems

Four fifth moves that are not 5.Nf3 with 6.Be2, and one recipe for each. They have one thing in common: White is trying to stop the plan of chapter 1 before it starts, by taking the centre with a fourth pawn, by putting a bishop on g5 before ...e5 can be played comfortably, or by spending a move on h3 so that the knight on f3 is never hit by ...Bg4 or ...Ng4. Black's answer changes with the system, and the chapter is about knowing which one you are in.

## The Four Pawns: 5.f4

White has four pawns in the centre and nothing behind them yet. The answer is not ...e5, which the pawn on f4 has been placed to meet, but 6...c5, hitting d4 from the side. After 7.d5 e6 the Benoni break comes at once, and after 8.Be2 exd5 9.cxd5 the bishop goes to g4 to trade the knight that holds e5 and d4. It is the one line in the course where Black gives up the bishop on c8 early and on purpose.

## The Averbakh: 5.Be2 O-O 6.Bg5

The bishop on g5 makes 6...e5 awkward, because 7.d5 and the pin on f6 stops ...f5 and the queen has to find a square. The knight goes to a6 first, then ...e5, and after d5 the queen goes to e8 to break the pin and hold e5. The knight on a6 goes to c5, the same square as chapter 1, and the plans are chapter 1's plans with the bishop on g5 as a target for ...h6 and ...Nh5.

## The h3 systems: 5.h3, and 5.Nf3 with 6.h3

The pawn on h3 takes g4 from Black and prepares g4 for White: the Makagonov idea is a pawn storm without castling. After 5.Nf3 O-O 6.h3 e5 7.d5 the knight goes to a6 and then to h5 and f4, because the bishop on e2 cannot take on h5 while the knight on f3 is in the way, and ...f5 follows. After 5.h3 with 6.Be3 the same ...e5 and ...Na6, and after 6.Bg5 the Benoni ...c5.

## 5.Nf3 with 6.Bd3, and 5.Bd3

The bishop on d3 is a move White will want back: it blocks the d-file and the queen. Against it the lever comes with a knight on c6, because d5 is met by ...Nd4 and the knight on d4 is a piece White has to spend a knight on.

## Typical mistakes at this level

Playing ...e5 against the Four Pawns, which is the move f4 was played to meet. Playing ...Nh5 when the bishop on e2 can take it: it works after h3 and Nf3 because the knight blocks the bishop, and not otherwise. Answering 6.Bg5 with ...h6 and ...g5, which loosens the king for a bishop that is happy on g3. And meeting the Makagonov's g4 with ...h6, which invites h4 and g5.

The break, with the knight on f4 in front of it and the queen on e8 behind. The pawn on e4 is hit and the knight on f4 is held by the pawn on e5.

mistakes.note: Sound: 12.Bxc5 dxc5 13.h4 and the pawn on c5 is doubled with the break still to come.
Sound: 12.a3 f5 and the same a move later.
12.g3 and the knight on f4 has to go back with the kingside opened.

children.plan: ...Nc5 and ...a5, ...fxe4 when Nxe4 can be met, ...Bd7 and ...Qe7. The knight on f4 is the best piece on the board and White has to spend g3 on it, which weakens f3 and h3 both.
children.name: 6.h3: the knight to f4

children.note: The bishop pins the knight.
Ask the bishop. It goes to e3, and the pawn on h6 is useful later.

mistakes.note: Sound: 9.Nd2 a5 and the same shape as chapter 1. The pawn first asks the bishop.
Sound: 9.Nd2 Nc5 and the pin is broken with the queen. The pawn on h6 does it with a pawn.

children.note: The bishop steps back to e3.
The knight to h5, with the knight on f3 blocking the bishop.

mistakes.note: Sound: 10.Nd2 a5 and the same. The knight to h5 uses the moment.

children.note: The knight to h2.
The queen to e8, holding h5.

mistakes.note: 11.Bxf4 exf4 12.Qd2 and the knight has been traded with the pawn on f4 loose.

children.plan: ...Nf4 after Be2, ...f5 behind it, ...Nc5 and ...a5. The same line with ...h6 played, which gives the knight on h5 a square on g7 and the king a hole on g6.
children.name: 6.h3 with 8.Bg5

children.note: White trades on e5, and there is a trick in it both ways.
Take back with the pawn.

mistakes.note: 8.Nxe4 dxe5 9.Qxd8 Rxd8 and two pawns for the knight.

children.note: The queens come off.
Take back with the rook.

mistakes.note: 9.Qxf8+ Bxf8 10.Nxe4 and a rook and a knight have gone for a pawn.

children.note: White takes the pawn, and it is a mistake: the knight on f6 takes on e4.
Take on e4. The knight on c3 takes back, and the bishop on g7 takes the knight on e5: the pawn is back and White's king is in the middle with the knight on e4 in the way of everything.

mistakes.note: 10.Nf3 and the pawn on e5 has gone for a tempo on nothing: the capture on e4 wins it back at once.
10.f4 and the pawn on e5 is held with the knight on f6 pinned to nothing: the capture first.

children.note: The knight takes back.
Take the knight. Level material, the bishop on e5 hitting b2, and White's king still on e1.

mistakes.note: 11.Nc3 and the knight on e5 is held with the pawn kept.

children.plan: ...Bxb2 if it is free, ...Nc6 and ...Be6 hitting c4, ...Rd4 against the knight on e4. The trade on e5 was a pawn White thought was free, and it was not.
children.name: 6.h3 and the ...Nxe4 trick

children.note: The bishop hits the knight that holds e5.
The rook off the pin and holding e5.

mistakes.note: Sound: 10.Nd5 c6 and the knight is pushed. The rook first.
10.Nd5 and the rook is hit.

children.note: The knight jumps in.
Take, and ...c6 undermines the pawn that arrives. With the king on e1 and no bishop on e2, 10...Nxe4 is not the trick it was in chapter 1: 11.Nxc7 hits both rooks.

mistakes.note: 11.Nxc7 and the knight forks the rooks: 11...Nxg5 12.Nxg5 Re7 13.Nxa8 and the exchange and a pawn have gone.
11.Nxc7 Rb8 12.Nxe8 and the exchange has gone: the knight on d5 had to be taken before it reached c7.

children.note: The pawn takes back.
Hit the wedge.

mistakes.note: 12.Be3 and the bishop on g7 is blocked by its own pawn.
Sound and slow: 12.O-O-O and White has the file.

children.plan: ...cxd5 and ...Nd7, ...Nc5 and ...Be6. The wedge comes off and the ending is level with Black's bishop the better one.
children.name: 6.h3 with 7.dxe5 and 9.Bg5

children.note: The bishop to d3, holding e4 and blocking the d-file: a move White will want back.
The lever. The bishop on d3 blocks the queen, so the trade on e5 is nothing to fear, and d5 is met by a knight on c6 that goes to d4.

mistakes.note: Sound: 7.Be2 Nfd7 and the bishop has asked the question. The lever keeps the shape.
Sound: 7.O-O e5 and the same a move later.
Sound: 7.d5 Ne5 8.Nxe5 dxe5 9.O-O and a closed centre where the knight that held d4 has been traded. The lever first keeps ...Na6 as the other choice.

children.note: White closes.
The pawn to a5, taking b4 from White and giving the knight on b8 the a6 square with c5 to follow.

mistakes.note: Sound, and it transposes after ...a5. The pawn first, because b4 was coming.
Sound: the bishop on d3 does not see h5, and 8.Nxe5 Bxe5 takes the knight back. The pawn on a5 first, because b4 is the plan.
8.dxc6 bxc6 9.Bg5 and the centre is loose with the pawn on d6 weak.

children.note: White castles.
The knight to a6 and c5, where it hits the bishop on d3.

mistakes.note: Sound: 9.Bc2 Nc5 and the same a move later. From a6 the knight keeps the bishop on c8 free.
Sound: 9.Nxe5 Bxe5 and the knight comes back. The knight on a6 first.

children.note: The pawn prepares b4 anyway.
The knight to c5, hitting the bishop on d3 and e4.

mistakes.note: Sound: the bishop on d3 does not see h5, and 10.Nxe5 Bxe5 takes the knight back. The knight to c5 first.
Sound: 10.b4 axb4 11.axb4 and the knight on a6 is hit next by b5. The knight first.

children.note: The bishop steps back to c2, holding e4 from behind.
The bishop out, and the queen's rook is connected for the a-file when b4 comes. The knight on f6 waits for the bishop on e2 that is not there: ...Nh5 is still met by Nxe5.

mistakes.note: 11.Nxe5 Bxe5 and the knight on h5 is safe, but the bishop on g7 has been drawn off the diagonal for nothing: the knight goes to h5 when there is something on f4 for it.
Sound: 11.Be3 and the pawn on a4 is held. The bishop first.

children.plan: ...a4 to fix b4, ...Ne8 and ...f5, ...Qe7 and ...Rfb8 for the a-file when b4 comes. The bishop on d3 has spent two moves getting to c2, where the knight on c5 keeps it honest.
children.name: 6.Bd3 with 7.d5

children.note: White castles and keeps the tension.
The knight to c6, hitting d4. With the bishop on d3 blocking the queen, 8.d5 is met by ...Nd4 and the knight on d4 costs White a knight to remove.

mistakes.note: Sound: 8.Re1 c6 and the same shape as chapter 1. The knight on c6 uses the bishop on d3 being in the way.
Sound: 8.Nxd4 Nc6 9.Nde2 and the open centre. The knight first keeps the pawn on e5.
8.d5 and the knight on d7 blocks the bishop with the centre closed on White's terms.

children.note: White closes, and the knight has d4.
The knight to d4. The bishop on d3 is in the way of the queen, so nothing takes it but the knight on f3, and 9.Nxd4 exd4 10.Ne2 gives Black a pawn on d4 that cramps everything.

mistakes.note: 9.Bg5 and the knight on e7 is pinned to the queen with the bishop on d3 doing its job.
9.Bb1 and the knight on b4 has nothing to hit.
Two moves lost: 9.Bg5 a5 10.Qd2 and White is ahead everywhere, though nothing has been lost yet.

children.note: The knight hits the knight on d4 from b5, offering a trade.
Take, and the pawn that lands on b5 is a target for ...a6 and the bishop that comes to d7.

mistakes.note: Sound: 10.Qxf3 a6 11.Nc3 and the knights have come off with the queen on f3. The knight on b5 first.
Sound: 10.a4 and the knight on d4 is held with the queenside fixed. The trade first keeps it simpler.

children.note: The pawn takes back.
The bishop to d7, hitting the pawn on b5 that has come too far. It is held by the bishop on d3 alone, and ...a6 next asks it.

mistakes.note: Sound: 11.bxa6 bxa6 and the b-file is Black's. The bishop first hits the pawn with a piece.
11.Nxe5 Bxe5 and the knight on h5 is safe, but the bishop on g7 has been drawn off the diagonal for nothing: the knight goes to h5 when there is something on f4 for it.

children.plan: ...a6 and ...Qe7, ...Ne8 and ...f5, with the pawn on b5 a target all game. The knight on d4 has been traded for the knight on c3 and White's queenside is loose.
children.name: 6.Bd3 with 7.O-O and ...Nd4

children.note: The knight takes.
Take back with the pawn, which sits on d4 hitting the knight on c3 and cramping the bishop on d3 and the queen both.

mistakes.note: 10.Bxe4 and the knight has gone for a pawn: the knight on d4 is safe behind the pawn on e5, which blocks the bishop on g7.

children.note: The knight steps back, hitting the pawn.
The rook to e8, hitting e4 through the knight: the pawn on d4 is held by the knight on f6 after ...Nd7 or by ...c5, and the pawn on e4 is the target.

mistakes.note: Sound: 11.dxc6 bxc6 and the pawn on d4 is held with the b-file open. The rook first.
11.Bxe4 and a knight has gone for a pawn: the bishop on d3 was holding it.

children.plan: ...c5 to hold the pawn on d4, ...Nd7 and ...Ne5 hitting the bishop, ...f5 against e4. The pawn on d4 is a wedge in White's camp and the knight on e2 is in its own way.
children.name: 6.Bd3 with 7.O-O and 9.Nxd4

tree.note: The bishop to d3 before the knight comes out, so that the knight can go to e2 and the f-pawn is free.

children.note: Castle.

mistakes.note: Sound: 6.Nge2 O-O and the same. The king first.
Sound: 6.d5 O-O 7.Nge2 and the same shape with the centre closed a move earlier.

children.note: The knight to e2, behind the bishop.
The knight to c6, hitting d4. With the knight on e2 and the bishop on d3, d5 is met by ...Nd4 and the knight on d4 sits on the knight on e2's only square to trade it.

mistakes.note: Sound: 7.d5 Nh5 8.Be3 Qh4 and the queen is out. The knight first hits d4 with a piece.
Sound: 7.d5 e6 and a Benoni. The knight keeps the lever.
Sound: 7.h3 e5 8.d5 Nd7 and the same shapes. The knight on c6 asks about d4 now.

children.note: White castles.
The lever, with the knight on c6 behind it and d4 hit twice.

mistakes.note: 8.Be3 e5 9.d5 and the knight on d7 blocks the bishop with the centre closed.
8.Be3 and the bishop has spent a move on nothing with d4 held.

children.note: White closes.
The knight to d4. The knight on e2 takes or the knight stays, and if it takes the pawn on d4 is a wedge the knight on e2 has to spend a move on.

mistakes.note: 9.f3 and the knight on e7 is in the way of the queen with White's storm ready.
9.Bb1 and the knight has nothing to hit.
Two moves lost: 9.Bg5 and White is ahead everywhere, though nothing has been lost yet.

children.note: The knight takes.
Take back with the pawn, which sits on d4 hitting the knight on c3.

mistakes.note: 10.Bxe4 and the knight has gone for a pawn: the pawn on e5 blocks the bishop on g7, so the knight on d4 is safe.

children.note: The knight steps back, hitting the pawn.
The rook to e8, hitting e4 through the knight.

mistakes.note: Sound: 11.dxc6 bxc6 and the pawn is held with the b-file open. The rook first.
11.Bxe4 and a knight has gone for a pawn.

children.note: The bishop pins the knight, which holds the pawn on d4.
Ask the bishop. It takes or goes back, and the pawn on d4 is held by ...c5 next in either case.

mistakes.note: Sound: 12.dxc6 bxc6 13.Bxf6 Qxf6 and the pawn on d4 is held by the queen. The pawn on h6 first.
12.Bxe4 and a knight has gone for a pawn.

children.note: The bishop takes the knight.
Take back with the queen, which holds d4 from f6 and sees the kingside. The bishop on g7 is kept and the pawn on d4 is held.

mistakes.note: 13.f4 and the pawn on d4 is held only by the bishop, which f5 will chase; the queen recapture holds d4 and keeps the bishop on g7.

children.plan: ...c5 to fix the pawn on d4, ...Bd7 and ...Re7 with ...Rae8 against e4, ...Qe5 when the queen wants the centre. The pawn on d4 is a wedge and White's knight on e2 is stuck holding it.
children.name: 5.Bd3 and 6.Nge2
